hero.headline: Three dead in shooting at Idaho fast food restaurant
hero.body:
Three people died in a shooting at an In-N-Out restaurant in Twin Falls, Idaho. Police responding to the scene found the body of the suspected gunman in an area near the restaurant, according to a city spokesman.

The shooting took place at the fast food chain location in Twin Falls. Five additional people were injured in the attack. Police have not released the identities of the victims or the suspected shooter.

The suspected gunman was found dead near the restaurant when officers arrived. Authorities have not disclosed how the shooter died or whether police fired any shots during their response.

In-N-Out owner expressed grief over the loss in a statement, referring to the shooting as the work of a person who does not value the lives of others or his own. The chain operates locations primarily in the western United States.

The shooting adds to a string of violent incidents at public locations across the country. Twin Falls police are investigating the circumstances that led to the attack and whether the shooter had any connection to the restaurant or its employees.

cards.headline: Trump Cancels Planned Iran Strikes, Cites Progress Toward Deal
cards.body:
President Trump announced he has canceled planned military strikes against Iran after receiving requests from Iranian and other Middle Eastern officials to pause military action. Trump said the decision was based on progress toward establishing what he called the "perimeters of a deal" with Tehran.

According to Trump, both Iran and leaders from other Middle Eastern countries asked the United States to hold off on any attack while negotiations advanced. The president tied the continuation of this pause directly to rapid progress in finalizing an agreement, suggesting the window for diplomacy may be limited.

While Trump claimed a deal could be signed very soon, possibly within days, he did not provide specific details about the terms being negotiated. His statements indicate that preliminary frameworks for a broader agreement have been established, though significant work remains to formalize any accord between Washington and Tehran.

The announcement represents a significant shift in the escalating confrontation between the two countries. Military strikes had apparently been planned and were close to execution before Trump decided to cancel them. The decision to pause military action in favor of diplomacy suggests a potential de-escalation, though the president's emphasis on rapid progress indicates the opening for negotiations may be brief.

Trump's approach appears conditional. He framed the cancellation as dependent on Iran moving quickly to conclude negotiations, leaving open the possibility of renewed military action if talks stall or produce no results within his stated timeframe.

The involvement of other Middle Eastern countries in requesting the pause suggests broader regional interest in preventing further conflict between the United States and Iran. This regional dimension adds complexity to the negotiations, as multiple parties appear invested in the outcome.

The announcement has drawn international attention as observers assess whether this opening will lead to a lasting agreement or prove temporary. The situation remains fluid, with Trump's conditional stance leaving significant uncertainty about the path forward.

The decision comes after months of escalating tensions between Washington and Tehran. Previous claims by Trump about imminent agreements with Iran have not materialized, making skepticism understandable among observers tracking these developments. The president's assertion that a deal could be signed imminently will require verification as events unfold.

How quickly negotiations progress in the coming days will be crucial in determining whether this represents a genuine breakthrough or another temporary pause in hostilities. Trump's insistence on speed suggests he views the current diplomatic window as narrow, and any slowdown could prompt a return to military action.

The international community will be watching closely to see whether the preliminary agreement on deal outlines can translate into a formal accord that satisfies all parties involved.

cards.headline: Trump cancels planned Iran strikes, cites progress in negotiations
cards.teaser: President Trump announced Saturday night he has called off potential military strikes on Iran after receiving requests from Middle Eastern nations to delay acti.
cards.body:
President Trump announced Saturday night he has called off potential military strikes on Iran after receiving requests from Middle Eastern nations to delay action. Trump said Iran and other countries in the region asked the United States to hold off any attack because the perimeters of a deal have been agreed to.

The decision comes amid heightened tensions between Washington and Tehran following Iran's missile strike on a US base in Jordan and continued disruption of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Some US officials had indicated that attacks on Iranian infrastructure were possible as leverage to push Iran toward accepting US terms in ceasefire negotiations.

Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman spoke with Trump on Saturday to express concern over plans for large-scale strikes against Iran, according to US officials and sources with knowledge of the call. Trump had been considering attacking Iranian energy targets in the coming days, though he had not issued final orders. Such an attack could lead to unpredictable escalation in the region.

Trump said in his statement that he agreed to cancel the attack for the future benefit of the world and the survival of a successful and prosperous Iran. The announcement indicates negotiations between the two nations have advanced, though Trump specified the cancellation was subject to being able to rapidly move forward on an agreement.

The development marks a significant shift in US policy toward Iran after weeks of rising military pressure. The administration had positioned potential strikes as a tool to force Iranian concessions in ongoing talks. Whether the diplomatic progress Trump referenced will translate into a lasting agreement remains to be seen.

cards.headline: Ferry Fire Off Indonesia Leaves Five Dead, 41 Missing
cards.teaser: A vessel carrying at least 250 people caught fire near Madura island, with dozens still unaccounted for.
cards.body:
A ferry carrying at least 250 passengers caught fire off the coast of Madura island in Indonesia. The incident resulted in five deaths and 41 people remain missing. Evacuation efforts were launched in the waters near the island as the fire spread across the vessel.

Rescue operations continue as authorities work to locate the missing passengers. Ferry accidents occur regularly in Indonesia, where maritime transport serves as a vital link connecting the nation's thousands of islands.

cards.headline: Five dead, 41 missing after Indonesia ferry fire
cards.teaser: A ferry carrying at least 250 people caught fire off the coast of Indonesia, leaving five dead and dozens missing.
cards.body:
Five people died and 41 remain missing after a ferry caught fire off Madura island in Indonesia. The vessel was carrying at least 250 people when the fire broke out.

Rescue operations are underway to locate the missing passengers. Ferry accidents occur with some frequency in Indonesia, an archipelago nation where maritime travel is common and safety regulations are not always consistently enforced.

cards.headline: Three killed in Moscow restaurant bombing
cards.teaser: A bomb exploded at a Moscow restaurant after a woman attempted to enter with explosives.
cards.body:
A homemade bomb killed three people and injured more than 20 others in an explosion near an Italian restaurant in central Moscow on Saturday evening. The blast occurred just before 8pm at Kudrinskaya Square, where the restaurant is located in one of Moscow's distinctive Stalin-era skyscrapers.

A woman carrying explosives attempted to enter the restaurant but was stopped by a security guard. The bomb detonated during the confrontation at the entrance. Russian authorities are investigating the incident and the circumstances surrounding it.

cards.headline: Far-Right Groups Plan Rally in Ceuta Demanding Migrant Expulsions
cards.teaser: Anti-immigration campaigners are organizing a demonstration in the Spanish territory following last week's mass border crossings.
cards.body:
Far-right leaders are calling for the expulsion of migrants remaining in Ceuta, the Spanish territory in North Africa. Anti-immigration campaigners planned a rally to demand stricter enforcement measures following a major border crossing.

An estimated 60,000 migrants from Morocco have crossed into Ceuta in one of the largest influxes in recent years. The mass crossing has intensified political pressure on Spanish authorities and fueled demands from right-wing groups for more aggressive deportation policies.

cards.headline: Most Migrants Who Entered Ceuta Have Returned to Morocco
cards.teaser: A small group remains on the seafront, tired and hungry, after the majority who surged across the border last week left.
cards.body:
Most of the migrants who crossed into Spain's North African territory of Ceuta from Morocco have returned. The massive influx occurred over 24 hours, with as many as 50,000 people entering the tiny enclave of 85,000 residents, overwhelming local resources and triggering a political crisis.

A small group of migrants remain sheltering on the beach, exhausted and hungry but determined to stay. The crossing has intensified tensions between Spain and Morocco, and sparked debate within the European Union over migration policy and border security.

cards.headline: Spain's Ceuta Migrant Crisis Exposes European Political Divisions
cards.teaser: The mass border crossings have shaken European politics and highlighted deep disagreements over immigration policy.
cards.body:
The migrant crossings into Ceuta have triggered significant political upheaval across Europe, laying bare deep divisions over migration policy. The crisis has resonated throughout the continent, shaking governments as they confront fundamental disagreements about how to address the influx.

Social media amplified the controversy surrounding the mass arrivals, with images and reports spreading rapidly across platforms. This digital spread intensified public debate and widened the political fallout, making migration a flashpoint in European discussions about border security and burden-sharing among member states.

cards.headline: US Restores Some Health Aid to Unicef, Gavi, and World Food Programme
cards.teaser: Funding for vaccine distribution and nutrition programs resumes, though at levels far below previous American contributions.
cards.body:
The United States has restored some vaccine and health aid to Unicef, Gavi, and the World Food Programme, resuming the flow of money for efforts to fight malnutrition and disease. The restored funding will support key humanitarian and health programs administered by the international organizations.

The amount allocated remains far below what the United States previously spent on humanitarian and health aid. The partial restoration comes after a period during which American contributions to these programs had been reduced or suspended. The organizations rely heavily on US funding to operate vaccination campaigns, nutrition programs, and emergency food distribution in vulnerable regions worldwide.

cards.headline: Venezuela's La Guaira Region Devastated a Month After Earthquakes
cards.teaser: The coastal area that once served as the country's main gateway remains unrecognizable more than a month after the disaster.
cards.body:
More than a month after earthquakes struck Venezuela, the coastal region of La Guaira is completely unrecognizable. The area, which once served as Venezuela's main gateway, has been transformed by the destruction from the seismic events.

The earthquakes caused widespread devastation across the coastal region, leaving infrastructure damaged and communities displaced. La Guaira's role as a critical port and entry point to the country has been severely disrupted by the disaster, with recovery efforts ongoing more than a month later.

cards.headline: Woman froze to death in Pittsburgh bus shelter
cards.teaser: Daphy Michel died after being found frozen in a Pittsburgh bus shelter.
cards.body:
Daphy Michel, a 31-year-old Haitian immigrant, froze to death in a Pittsburgh bus shelter in early March after being released from ICE custody. She was dropped off in the city in 20-degree weather wearing only summer clothes. Michel had spent six months in county jail following a reported mental health crisis, then was arrested by ICE before her release with an ankle monitor.

Her family is preparing to sue the United States and multiple governmental and non-governmental entities over her death. Michel was known by those close to her for showing love to everyone around her.

cards.headline: Parasite sickens thousands across U.S. this summer
cards.teaser: Cyclospora has caused illness in thousands of people in the United States during recent months.
cards.body:
Cyclospora, a parasite infecting thousands of Americans this summer, spreads through contaminated food and water. The organism requires time in the human digestive tract to reproduce and causes gastrointestinal illness.

Cyclospora infections typically produce diarrhea, loss of appetite, and other digestive symptoms lasting weeks without treatment. The outbreak represents a significant public health concern across the country.

cards.headline: Mountaineer Nirmal Purja's body recovered after Pakistan avalanche
cards.teaser: The body of renowned climber Nirmal Purja has been found following an avalanche in Pakistan.
cards.body:
The body of renowned mountaineer Nirmal Purja was recovered following an avalanche in Pakistan. Purja had gained international acclaim for climbing all 14 of the world's peaks above 8,000 meters in just over six months in 2019, setting a record for the fastest ascent of these mountains.

Purja was part of an international mountaineering team attempting to climb one of Earth's tallest peaks when the avalanche struck. The expedition included climbers from multiple countries, including the United States.

cards.headline: Spain faces political divide over migrant crossings
cards.teaser: Migrant arrivals in Ceuta have created political tensions in Spain and across Europe.
cards.body:
Migrant crossings into Ceuta, Spain's North African enclave, have triggered a political crisis that has reverberated across Europe. The arrivals have exposed deep divisions among European governments over how to handle migration, an increasingly contentious policy issue.

Social media has intensified the political fallout from the Ceuta crossings, amplifying debate and spreading the controversy beyond Spain's borders. The situation has become a focal point for wider European discussions about border security and asylum policies.

hero.headline: California Lettuce Farmers Destroy Crops as Cyclospora Outbreak Tanks Demand
hero.body:
California lettuce farmers are plowing under fields of healthy crops as demand for fresh greens collapses in response to a nationwide cyclospora outbreak. The parasite, which causes severe gastrointestinal illness, has been detected in at least 34 states, with Michigan reporting more than 5,000 confirmed cases alone.

The outbreak has been traced to Taylor Farms, a major produce supplier. The company recalled shredded iceberg lettuce grown at its facility in Guanajuato, Mexico, distributed across 27 states as recently as Thursday. Taylor Farms products reach major retailers including Costco, Target, and Walmart, as well as organic brands like Earthbound Farm. The FDA has also identified contaminated products served at Taco Bell locations in Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio, and West Virginia, with more than 1,600 cases linked to the same product.

The scale of this outbreak far exceeds typical summer cyclospora cases. Last year, the entire US saw only 249 confirmed cases total. This year's numbers represent a dramatic spike, though health officials warn that actual infections may continue rising for at least another two weeks.

The destruction of ready-to-harvest lettuce represents a significant financial loss for growers who invested months of labor and resources into the crops. Fear of contamination has driven shoppers away from commercial lettuce, despite the outbreak being traced to a specific supplier and growing region.

Cyclospora is a parasite that contaminates food through contact with fecal matter, often via contaminated water used for irrigation or washing. The illness it causes includes severe diarrhea, stomach cramps, nausea, and fatigue that can last for weeks without treatment.

The economic impact extends beyond individual farms. The crisis has disrupted the supply chain for fresh greens, affecting distributors, retailers, and food service operations. Taco Bell was the first restaurant to announce it would stop serving produce in several affected states. The outbreak arrives during peak growing season for lettuce in California, which produces the majority of fresh greens consumed in the United States.

The recall has created confusion among consumers and retailers. Taylor Farms did not specify the brand names of recalled products or where they were served and sold, complicating efforts to identify contaminated items. The FDA has warned that "additional implicated brands, restaurants, retailers, or distribution channels may be identified as the investigation continues."

This is not Taylor Farms' first serious food safety incident. In 2013, the company was linked to a cyclospora outbreak at restaurants including the Olive Garden and Red Lobster. In October 2024, an E. coli outbreak linked to McDonald's Quarter Pounders was traced to the producer's slivered onions.

Public health authorities continue investigating the source while the industry awaits clarity on which products remain safe.

cards.headline: SpaceX Faces Investor Scrutiny Ahead of First Earnings Report
cards.teaser: SpaceX prepares to release financial results for the first time as investors ask questions ranging from technical challenges to business strategy.
cards.body:
SpaceX is preparing to report earnings to investors for the first time. The company is navigating questions that span technical challenges with its Starship vehicle alongside more unconventional investor inquiries, including potential rocket paint colors.

The earnings announcement comes as SpaceX's stock has declined significantly to record lows. The timing coincides with a lockup period expiration and continued development hurdles for Starship. Analysts are monitoring how the company will address both its near-term financial performance and longer-term objectives.

cards.headline: California Governor Raises Concerns About Paramount-Warner Bros. Antitrust Suit
cards.teaser: Governor Gavin Newsom has expressed reservations about California's antitrust lawsuit challenging the proposed merger between Paramount and Warner Bros.
cards.body:
Newsom has voiced concerns about the state's legal action against the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger, according to reports. The lawsuit, brought by California and other state attorneys general, seeks to block the combination of the two major entertainment companies on antitrust grounds. The parties are currently disputing the trial schedule.

The potential collapse of the merger would cost the Ellison family $9.8 billion. Paramount and the state attorneys general are engaged in legal wrangling over procedural matters as the case moves forward. The governor's reported concerns add a new dimension to the high-stakes legal battle over one of the largest proposed media mergers in recent years.

cards.headline: Paul Weiss Law Firm Reverses Course on Trump Opposition
cards.teaser: The law firm Paul Weiss, which led legal challenges against President Trump during his first term, has shifted its stance under White House pressure.
cards.body:
Paul Weiss abandoned its opposition to President Trump after decades as a progressive institution and leader of the legal resistance during Trump's first term. The firm's transformation represents a broader retreat across the legal industry in response to pressure from the White House. The reversal marks a significant shift for a firm that had been a stalwart of resistance to Trump's policies.

The capitulation reflects changing dynamics between major law firms and the current administration. Paul Weiss had taken prominent roles in challenging Trump administration actions but has now withdrawn from that position. The firm's decision has prompted examination of how corporate legal practices navigate political pressure and client relationships.

cards.headline: Wealthy Individuals Relocate to Miami, Drawing Financial Firms
cards.teaser: The ultra-rich are moving to Miami in growing numbers, creating demand for wealth management firms to establish operations in the city.
cards.body:
Tax incentives and other benefits have attracted wealthy individuals to Miami, spurring demand for local offices of firms that manage their money. The migration of high-net-worth individuals to the city is reshaping the financial services landscape in South Florida. Wealth managers are following their clients to establish or expand Miami operations.

The trend reflects broader population and wealth shifts toward Florida, which offers favorable tax treatment compared to high-tax states. Money management firms that previously operated primarily in traditional financial centers are now seeking office space in Miami to serve relocated clients. The influx has implications for commercial real estate and the local financial services industry.

cards.headline: More College Graduates Living With Parents Amid Weak Job Market
cards.teaser: An increasing share of young college graduates are living at home with their parents, suggesting challenges in the job market but reduced social stigma.
cards.body:
More young adults with college degrees are living with their parents, a trend that points to weakness in the job market for recent graduates. The increase suggests that new degree holders face difficulty finding employment that allows independent living. Experts note the development also reflects reduced social stigma around returning home after college.

The phenomenon indicates economic pressures on young workers, including housing costs and entry-level wages that may not support independent living in many markets. While previous generations viewed living with parents after college as undesirable, current graduates appear more willing to accept the arrangement. The trend has implications for housing demand, consumer spending, and workforce mobility among young professionals.

cards.headline: Powerball Jackpot Grows to $748 Million After No Winner
cards.teaser: The Powerball jackpot increased to $748 million after no ticket matched all numbers, while a Los Angeles gas station sold a ticket worth $809,000.
cards.body:
The Powerball jackpot reached $748 million following the August 1 drawing, which produced no grand prize winner. A ticket sold at a gas station in Los Angeles won $809,000 by matching five numbers while missing the Powerball.

With no jackpot winner, the prize will roll over to the next drawing. Lottery officials anticipate increased ticket sales as the jackpot continues to grow.

hero.headline: Minnesota ban on nudify apps moves forward after judge denies xAI request
hero.body:
A federal judge rejected xAI's legal challenge to Minnesota's ban on applications that create fake nude images, allowing the state restriction to move forward. The decision represents a significant victory for state regulators attempting to address harms created by artificial intelligence technology.

The Minnesota law targets nudify apps, which use AI to digitally remove clothing from photos of people without their consent. The state legislature passed the measure in response to growing concerns about nonconsensual intimate imagery generated through AI. xAI filed a lawsuit seeking to block enforcement of the ban, but the court denied the company's request for a preliminary injunction.

The denial of xAI's request means Minnesota can proceed with implementing and enforcing penalties against developers and distributors offering nudify technology within the state. The ruling reflects broader efforts by state governments to regulate AI applications they consider harmful, particularly those that create deepfake content or synthetic intimate imagery.

The case highlights ongoing tensions between technology companies and state regulators over AI regulation. Several states have already moved to restrict deepfake technology and nonconsensual synthetic media. Minnesota joins these jurisdictions in establishing legal frameworks specifically targeting AI-enabled image manipulation.

Advocates for the ban have pointed to the disproportionate impact of such apps on women and minors. Nonconsensual intimate imagery created through AI tools has become an increasing concern for lawmakers and privacy advocates nationwide. The technology allows bad actors to create convincing fake nude images of real people, often without their knowledge or permission.

The judge's decision to uphold the ban suggests courts are willing to support state efforts to regulate AI in ways that protect individuals from specific harms. This ruling comes as the Trump administration and state governments continue debating the appropriate scope of AI regulation and who should control such policy.

xAI, owned by billionaire Elon Musk, has not publicly detailed the specific legal arguments it made against Minnesota's nudify app ban. The company's challenge apparently focused on constitutional or regulatory grounds, but the court found those arguments insufficient to block the law's enforcement.

The outcome may influence other states considering similar restrictions on AI-generated intimate imagery. As more jurisdictions implement their own AI regulations, technology companies will likely face additional legal battles over restrictions on their tools and services.

The ruling allows Minnesota to begin enforcing the law while any further legal proceedings continue. State officials have yet to fully detail how they will implement enforcement mechanisms or what penalties app developers and distributors will face for violating the ban.

cards.headline: Apple faces challenges managing AI-driven bug reports
cards.teaser: The company's bug bounty program is struggling to process submissions generated with artificial intelligence tools.
cards.body:
Apple is encountering difficulties keeping up with security researchers using AI to find and report software vulnerabilities. The surge in AI-assisted bug hunting has created a wave of submissions that the company's existing processes are struggling to handle.

The bug bounty program, which rewards researchers for identifying security flaws, has seen an increase in reports generated or aided by large language models and other AI tools. This has created challenges for Apple's security teams in reviewing and validating the influx of findings.

cards.headline: YouTuber Hank Green says his AI use is unhealthy
cards.teaser: The content creator apologized for what he described as excessive interaction with large language models.
cards.body:
Hank Green has publicly apologized for his use of AI, acknowledging that interacting with large language models triggers excessive dopamine responses that he considers unhealthy for himself and society.

The YouTuber's candid admission highlights potential addictive qualities in AI chatbot interactions, specifically pointing to the neurochemical reward mechanisms activated during these conversations as a concern.

cards.headline: Beaver reintroduction creates wetlands, improves drought resilience
cards.teaser: New research documents how reintroduced beavers are expanding wetland areas in their habitats.
cards.body:
Beavers brought back to wild habitats are creating more wetland areas through their dam-building activity, according to recent research. The findings show that beaver engineering is contributing to increased water retention and habitat diversity in reintroduction zones.

The study documents ecological changes following beaver reintroduction programs, with the animals' natural dam construction expanding wetland acreage. These wetland areas provide benefits for drought resilience by storing water during dry periods and supporting diverse ecosystems.

cards.headline: Apple signals September keynote for iPhone 18 Pro
cards.teaser: An update to Apple's event scheduling suggests the next iPhone model will debut in September.
cards.body:
Apple has indicated a September release timeframe for the iPhone 18 Pro through updates to its keynote calendar. The scheduling information points to a continuation of the company's traditional fall launch window for new iPhone models.

Reports also suggest the upcoming iPhone 18 line may see price increases compared to previous generations. Additional rumors point to potential features including a smaller Dynamic Island design, increased RAM configurations, and a new A20 chip built on a smaller manufacturing process.

cards.headline: Mars surface temperatures span wide range within standing height
cards.teaser: The planet's thin atmosphere allows ground and air temperatures to differ drastically at the same location.
cards.body:
Mars' thin atmosphere creates stark temperature contrasts between the ground and air. Near the equator at noon, sunlit ground can reach 24 degrees Celsius while the air at head height remains below freezing.

This extreme difference occurs because Mars' sparse atmosphere transfers very little heat from the warm surface to the air above. A person standing on Mars could experience spring-like warmth at their feet while their head experiences freezing temperatures.

cards.headline: August brings partial solar and lunar eclipses
cards.teaser: Skywatchers can observe two partial eclipses this month along with peak meteor shower activity.
cards.body:
Two partial eclipses will occur in August, offering viewing opportunities for astronomy enthusiasts. The month features both a partial solar eclipse and a partial lunar eclipse as part of an eclipse season.

August 12 has been highlighted as a particularly active day for skywatching, with multiple celestial events coinciding. The month also includes the peak of the Perseid meteor shower and potential northern lights visibility in some regions.

hero.headline: Dodgers acquire ace Tarik Skubal from Tigers in blockbuster trade
hero.body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have acquired left-handed pitcher Tarik Skubal from the Detroit Tigers in a major trade deadline deal. The blockbuster move brings one of baseball's top starting pitchers to the National League West leaders as they push toward the playoffs.

Skubal, who has emerged as an ace for Detroit, delivered an emotional farewell to the Tigers organization. The 29-year-old left-hander fought back tears as he said goodbye to the team that developed him into one of the game's premier pitchers. The trade marks a significant shift for both franchises, with the Dodgers adding frontline pitching talent while the Tigers focus on building for the future.

The Tigers received multiple prospects in return for their star pitcher, though the full details of the package were not immediately disclosed. The deal represents one of the most significant moves at this year's trade deadline, as contending teams scrambled to add impact players before the cutoff. For Detroit, trading Skubal signals a commitment to a rebuild centered around younger talent.

The acquisition addresses a key need for Los Angeles as they aim to strengthen their rotation for the stretch run. Skubal joins a Dodgers pitching staff that will now feature one of the deepest collections of starting talent in the majors. His addition gives manager Dave Roberts another high-caliber arm to deploy in crucial games down the stretch and into October.

The trade sent ripples through the rest of the deadline market, influencing how other teams approached their own negotiations. With one of the top available pitchers now off the board, remaining contenders adjusted their strategies in the final hours before the deadline. The Dodgers' willingness to part with prospects to land an established ace underscores their championship aspirations for this season.

cards.headline: White Sox acquire Luis Castillo from Mariners in three-player trade
cards.teaser: Chicago added starting pitcher Luis Castillo in a four-player deal with Seattle.
cards.body:
The Chicago White Sox acquired starting pitcher Luis Castillo from the Seattle Mariners in a trade involving three players heading to Seattle. The deal adds a proven starter to the White Sox rotation as they look to bolster their pitching staff.

The Mariners shed salary in the transaction while receiving multiple players in return. The trade represents a shift in direction for Seattle, which moved one of its more expensive contracts as part of the deadline activity.

cards.headline: Sparks trade All-Star guard Kelsey Plum to Phoenix Mercury
cards.teaser: Los Angeles dealt its All-Star guard to Phoenix in a blockbuster WNBA deadline move.
cards.body:
The Los Angeles Sparks traded All-Star guard Kelsey Plum to the Phoenix Mercury ahead of the WNBA trade deadline. The move sends one of the league's top guards to a division rival in a significant shakeup for both franchises.

Plum had planned to return to the Sparks on Sunday before the trade was finalized. The deal marks one of the most notable transactions at this year's deadline, as teams navigated the new collective bargaining agreement's impact on roster construction.

cards.headline: Yankees trade reliever Camilo Doval to Pirates for two prospects
cards.teaser: New York dealt the struggling reliever to Pittsburgh in exchange for catcher Omar Alfonzo and outfielder Luis Cruz.
cards.body:
The New York Yankees traded relief pitcher Camilo Doval to the Pittsburgh Pirates, receiving catcher Omar Alfonzo and outfielder Luis Cruz in return. Doval had fallen in the Yankees bullpen hierarchy, prompting the organization to move the right-hander.

The Pirates take on a high-upside arm who had struggled with New York but could rebound in a new environment. For the Yankees, the trade clears a roster spot while adding two prospects to their farm system as they reshape their bullpen.

cards.headline: Braves acquire Lane Thomas and Bailey Falter from Royals
cards.teaser: Atlanta added outfielder Lane Thomas and left-handed reliever Bailey Falter in a four-player trade with Kansas City.
cards.body:
The Atlanta Braves acquired outfielder Lane Thomas and left-handed reliever Bailey Falter from the Kansas City Royals in a four-player trade. The deal brings additional depth to the Braves outfield and bullpen as they pursue a playoff spot.

The trade sends two players to Kansas City as part of the deadline exchange. Thomas provides Atlanta with another bat and defensive option in the outfield, while Falter adds a left-handed arm to the bullpen mix for the stretch run.

cards.headline: Alexandra Eala defeats Naomi Osaka to reach Washington Open final
cards.teaser: The rising star continued her strong season with a victory over the four-time Grand Slam champion.
cards.body:
Alexandra Eala secured an impressive victory over Naomi Osaka to advance to the Washington Open final. The win caps a strong season for the rising player, who continues to establish herself as a prominent force on the tour.

Eala's triumph over the four-time Grand Slam champion represents a significant milestone in her career. She will now compete for the Washington Open title in the final.

cards.headline: Australia defeats England 68-50 for Commonwealth Games netball bronze
cards.teaser: England fell short in their bid for a bronze medal at the Commonwealth Games.
cards.body:
Australia outclassed England 68-50 in the bronze medal match at the Commonwealth Games netball tournament. The decisive victory secured the Australians third place on the podium.

England's medal hopes ended after losing to New Zealand 61-54 in the semifinals. The defeat meant the Roses faced Australia in the bronze medal match, where they were unable to mount a challenge against the more dominant side.

hero.headline: Sopranos Actor Vincent Pastore Dies at 80
hero.body:
Vincent Pastore, the actor known for playing mobster Salvatore "Big Pussy" Bonpensiero on The Sopranos, has died at age 80. His former castmates remembered him in tributes shared on social media following the announcement of his death.

Pastore appeared on The Sopranos during its groundbreaking early seasons on HBO, portraying a member of Tony Soprano's crew. His character became one of the show's most memorable figures before meeting a dramatic end in the series. The role cemented Pastore's reputation for playing tough guys and mobsters throughout his career.

Castmates from The Sopranos mourned Pastore on social media, describing him as a beloved friend and beautiful soul. The tributes highlighted both his professional contributions to the iconic series and his personal relationships with fellow actors from the show. Page Six reported that cast members expressed grief over losing someone they had worked closely with during the show's run.

The timing of Pastore's death coincided with another Sopranos cast member singing the national anthem at a Mets game, creating an unexpected contrast between celebration and mourning for the show's family of actors. CNN and BBC covered the news of his passing, noting his decades-long career playing characters that became synonymous with his name in popular culture.

Pastore's death marks another loss for the cast of The Sopranos, which has seen several members pass away in recent years. The show, which ended its run in 2007, continues to be regarded as one of television's most influential series, and Pastore's performance remains a significant part of its legacy.

cards.headline: British Filmmaker Dies Before Wicker Man Sequel Premiere
cards.teaser: The son of the original Wicker Man director died after a heart attack just weeks before his sequel to the film was set to premiere.
cards.body:
A British filmmaker died on Friday after suffering a heart attack, according to a statement from his family. The director was the son of the maker of the original Wicker Man film.

His death occurred just weeks before the premiere of his sequel to the classic horror film. The family confirmed the cause of death in their statement but did not provide additional details about the circumstances.

cards.headline: Modest Mouse Removes Guitarist After Allegations of Inappropriate Messages to Minor
cards.teaser: The band dismissed guitarist Simon O'Connor from their tour following allegations that he sent inappropriate messages to a teenage fan.
cards.body:
Modest Mouse removed guitarist Simon O'Connor from their current tour after allegations surfaced that he sent inappropriate messages to a minor. The band was scheduled to perform at the Outside Lands music festival when they made the decision to part ways with O'Connor.

O'Connor issued an apology for the inappropriate messages sent to the underage fan. Multiple outlets reported on the dismissal as the band prepared for their upcoming festival appearance in San Francisco.

cards.headline: Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman Appear at Practical Magic Screening
cards.teaser: The two stars surprised fans at a screening of their 1998 film at Hollywood Forever Cemetery.
cards.body:
Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman made an unannounced appearance at a screening of Practical Magic at Hollywood Forever Cemetery in Los Angeles. The event was hosted by Cinespia, which organizes film screenings at the cemetery venue.

The actors introduced the 1998 film to attendees who had gathered for the outdoor screening. Kidman later posted a photo of herself and Bullock on social media. The appearance comes amid news of a sequel to the cult classic film and a new deluxe edition of the original novel by author Alice Hoffman.

cards.headline: WWE's Oba Femi Defeats Brock Lesnar at SummerSlam
cards.teaser: The rising wrestler defeated the veteran star in a Hell in a Cell match at the pay-per-view event.
cards.body:
Oba Femi defeated Brock Lesnar at WWE SummerSlam in what commentators described as a torch-passing moment for the company. The match took place inside a Hell in a Cell cage during the first night of the two-day event.

The victory positions Femi as part of what Bleacher Report called the start of WWE's next era. The brutal match between the two wrestlers was characterized as an attempt by both competitors to destroy each other. Questions about Lesnar's future with WWE have emerged following the loss.

cards.headline: SmackDown GM Nick Aldis Makes In-Ring Debut at SummerSlam
cards.teaser: The WWE executive competed in a match against Gunther during the pay-per-view event.
cards.body:
Nick Aldis, the general manager of WWE's SmackDown brand, made an in-ring debut at SummerSlam in a match against Gunther. The executive was forced to tap out during the bout at the AMC venue.

Multiple wrestling outlets reported on Aldis's impressive performance despite the loss. The match marked a return to active competition for Aldis, who had been serving in an administrative role for the SmackDown brand. His future with the company following the match has been the subject of wrestling news coverage.

cards.headline: Lioness Returns for Third Season on Paramount Plus
cards.teaser: The series starring Nicole Kidman and Zoe Saldana premiered its latest season.
cards.body:
The third season of Lioness debuted on Paramount Plus, with stars Nicole Kidman and Zoe Saldana returning for new episodes. The military-themed drama series premiered at an event attended by the lead actors.

Actresses Jill Wagner and Laysla De Oliveira received praise from military personnel for the show's accuracy. Creator Taylor Sheridan is returning for an on-camera role in the new season. Page Six published information about how viewers can watch the new episodes.

hero.headline: Trump administration ends Medicare drug subsidy program
hero.teaser: A subsidy program that helped keep costs down for Medicare drug coverage has ended, potentially leaving millions of seniors with higher monthly costs.
hero.body:
The Trump administration has ended a subsidy program that helped reduce costs for Medicare drug coverage. The move could result in higher monthly expenses for millions of seniors enrolled in the program.

The decision appears to work against the administration's message on drug affordability. President Trump frequently promotes his push for access to cheaper drugs through the TrumpRx platform and making most-favored-nation deals with other countries.

cards.headline: Trump cancels planned Iran strikes, cites progress in negotiations
cards.teaser: President Trump announced Saturday night he has called off potential military strikes on Iran after receiving requests from Middle Eastern nations to delay acti.
cards.body:
President Trump announced Saturday night he has called off potential military strikes on Iran after receiving requests from Middle Eastern nations to delay action. Trump said Iran and other countries in the region asked the United States to hold off any attack because the perimeters of a deal have been agreed to.

The decision comes amid heightened tensions between Washington and Tehran following Iran's missile strike on a US base in Jordan and continued disruption of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Some US officials had indicated that attacks on Iranian infrastructure were possible as leverage to push Iran toward accepting US terms in ceasefire negotiations.

Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman spoke with Trump on Saturday to express concern over plans for large-scale strikes against Iran, according to US officials and sources with knowledge of the call. Trump had been considering attacking Iranian energy targets in the coming days, though he had not issued final orders. Such an attack could lead to unpredictable escalation in the region.

Trump said in his statement that he agreed to cancel the attack for the future benefit of the world and the survival of a successful and prosperous Iran. The announcement indicates negotiations between the two nations have advanced, though Trump specified the cancellation was subject to being able to rapidly move forward on an agreement.

The development marks a significant shift in US policy toward Iran after weeks of rising military pressure. The administration had positioned potential strikes as a tool to force Iranian concessions in ongoing talks. Whether the diplomatic progress Trump referenced will translate into a lasting agreement remains to be seen.

cards.headline: Justice Department drops vandalism case against former Olympian
cards.teaser: The DOJ moved to dismiss its felony charge against David Hearn after finding evidence that faulty construction, not vandalism, damaged the Reflecting Pool.
cards.body:
The Justice Department on Friday moved to dismiss its felony destruction of property charge against former Olympian David Hearn. The department found that faulty construction was responsible for damage to the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, not vandalism as originally alleged.

Democrats responded to the dismissal by saying it validated their longstanding criticism that the administration is weaponizing the Justice Department. Interior Secretary Doug Burgum rejected the DOJ's assessment, maintaining that vandals were responsible for the damage to the Reflecting Pool.

cards.headline: Democratic Socialists consider presidential endorsement at summit
cards.teaser: The Democratic Socialists of America discussed whether to endorse a presidential candidate, with Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez mentioned as a potential option.
cards.body:
Delegates at the Democratic Socialists of America summit discussed the possibility of endorsing a presidential candidate. The conversation centered on whether the organization should formally back a candidate in the upcoming election cycle.

Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez emerged as a potential endorsement candidate during the discussions. The summit highlighted growing interest among democratic socialists in directly engaging with presidential politics rather than focusing solely on down-ballot races.

cards.headline: Alaska Senate race features two candidates named Dan Sullivan
cards.teaser: Sen. Dan Sullivan faces a primary challenge from another Dan Sullivan after a judge ruled the candidate with the same name can remain on the ballot.
cards.body:
Sen. Dan Sullivan is running for reelection in Alaska and faces a primary challenge from Dan Sullivan. An Alaska judge ruled in June that a candidate with the same name and party affiliation as the incumbent Republican can stay on the ballot.

Early voting begins in the state Monday. The incumbent's full name is Dan S. Sullivan, while his challenger shares both the same name and Republican party affiliation, creating potential confusion for voters in the Senate primary.

cards.headline: Trump administration works to implement Hamas disarmament deal
cards.teaser: President Trump announced a historic deal with negotiators that includes disarming Hamas, though skeptics question whether it can be implemented.
cards.body:
President Trump announced a deal reached with negotiators this week that includes disarming Hamas as part of efforts to reach a ceasefire in Gaza. The agreement is part of Trump's 20-point plan to end the war between Israel and Hamas.

The deal faces implementation challenges as skeptics wonder if it can move from paper to reality. The agreement represents a test for the Trump administration as it attempts to broker a lasting ceasefire in the Gaza Strip.

cards.headline: Michigan Democrats worry about progressive primary challengers
cards.teaser: Mainstream Democrats express concern that progressive victories in two Michigan primaries could affect the party's chances in November congressional races.
cards.body:
Mainstream Democrats are expressing concern about progressive candidates Abdul El-Sayed and Will Lawrence, who are competing in Michigan primary races on Tuesday. Both candidates are backed by Sen. Bernie Sanders for their respective Senate and House primaries.

Center-left Democrats worry that progressive victories could jeopardize the party's chances of winning congressional seats in November. The primaries are seen as critical races in Michigan, a state considered essential for Democrats in the general election.
